doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His father's open mind toward improvisers
summary: Although a classical player, his father valued improvisers, in contrast to the tradition that is only slowly changing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: And even more than that, your father was an orchestral player.
But obviously from what you told us yesterday, he appreciated the art of the improvisers.
He knew how to appreciate that.
He didn’t find that to be obtuse, or something that needed to be avoided.

Yea. So, it is changing little by little, but tradition is still there. And that’s why that trombonist had a terror face when I asked him to play one note [imitates not]; one note, that’s all. I was not asking him to play the Mozart concerto for clarinet on the trombone [imitates note], but for him that was like seeing a monster or something, you know.
